CONCURRENT CROSS-TEAM WRITES are not serialized: two dispatch passes for two teams that both run across their own `await send(...)` can still lose a row at the final whole-file write (the T7 merge narrows the window but is per-pass). This is the pre-existing single-file ledger race, not introduced by R1 — one file, no lock.

The turn-boundary listener scans the workspace's team records on every turn-stopping event (the same scan mpd-team-compact-plugin already performs on that event). Settlement lands only for a session whose executorRef is on a roster.

designNotes: readLedger/writeLedger stay FILE-level (workspace only): they are the one atomic-file seam, and a team-scoped READ would make every writer merge rows it never read. The teamId is threaded through the PURE helpers they feed (reconcile/ledgerOfTeam/assign/release/forgetTeam) and through both tools, which is where the scoping can be enforced without a lossy write.

The terminal-phase prune is anchored on the reap's OWN report: reapReapedTeams (team-lifecycle.ts) is the terminal write path, and its returned ids are what the dispatch run hands to forgetTeam. No second terminal write path exists (grep: `phase: "ended"` is written in exactly one place).

The phase is re-derived on BOTH claim paths (agent_teams_task claim and the dispatch claim) because settlement makes `idle -> active` reachable; without it the stored phase could disagree with a running member/task row.
